headers: Why CIA is involved / what must be protected

items.Title: AI risk assessment
items.Security requirement: Define and apply an AI risk assessment process: risk criteria, consistent/valid/comparable results, identify risks, analyse potential consequences and likelihood, evaluate and prioritise; retain documented information.
items.Why CIA is involved / what must be prote: Cover AI-specific threats: data poisoning, model theft/inversion, adversarial inputs, prompt injection, supply chain.
items.Evidence to verify: AI risk methodology, AI risk register and assessments
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI risk treatment
items.Security requirement: Define AI risk treatment process: select options, determine necessary controls (compare with Annex A), produce Statement of Applicability with justification, formulate treatment plan, obtain approval and residual risk acceptance.
items.Why CIA is involved / what must be prote: Select security controls; compare with ISO 27001 Annex A in SoA.
items.Evidence to verify: AI risk treatment plan, SoA, residual risk sign-off
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Control of documented information
items.Security requirement: Control availability, protection, distribution, access, storage, version control, retention and disposition; control external-origin documents.
items.Why CIA is involved / what must be prote: Protect confidentiality/integrity/availability of AIMS documents (models, data docs).
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI risk assessment
items.Security requirement: Perform AI risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed/occur; retain results.
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI risk treatment
items.Security requirement: Implement the AI risk treatment plan and retain results of treatment.
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Tooling resources
items.Security requirement: Document tooling resources used for the AI system (algorithms, models, libraries, frameworks, MLOps).
items.Why CIA is involved / what must be prote: Secure AI libraries, frameworks, model artifacts, MLOps pipeline.
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: System and computing resources
items.Security requirement: Document system and computing resources used (hardware, cloud, compute, storage).
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Processes for responsible AI system design and development
items.Security requirement: Define and document specific processes for responsible design and development of AI systems.
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: AI system requirements and specification
items.Security requirement: Specify and document requirements for new AI systems or material enhancements.
items.Why CIA is involved / what must be prote: Security requirements and threat modelling for AI.
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: AI system verification and validation
items.Security requirement: Define and document verification/validation measures and criteria (performance, bias, robustness, security testing).
items.Evidence to verify: Test plans, V&V reports, acceptance criteria
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: AI system deployment
items.Security requirement: Document a deployment plan and ensure appropriate requirements are met before deployment.
items.Why CIA is involved / what must be prote: Secure release, change approval, environment separation.
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: AI system operation and monitoring
items.Security requirement: Define and document elements for ongoing operation: system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support.
items.Evidence to verify: Monitoring dashboards, drift/performance alerts, update procedures
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: AI system recording of event logs
items.Security requirement: Determine at which phases of the life cycle event logs should be enabled, at minimum when the system is in use.
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Quality of data for AI systems
items.Security requirement: Define and document data quality requirements and ensure data used meets them.
items.Evidence to verify: Data quality criteria and check results
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Data provenance
items.Security requirement: Define and document a process for recording provenance of data (and its updates) throughout the life cycle.
items.Why CIA is involved / what must be prote: Traceability and integrity of data lineage.
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Communication of incidents
items.Security requirement: Determine and document a plan for communicating incidents to users and other interested parties (incl. regulators).
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Allocating responsibilities
items.Security requirement: Ensure responsibilities within the AI life cycle are allocated between the organization, partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Suppliers
items.Security requirement: Establish a process to ensure supplier services, products or materials align with the organization's responsible AI approach.
items.Why CIA is involved / what must be prote: Supplier security due diligence, contracts, monitoring.
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Understanding the organization and its context
items.Requirement: Determine external/internal issues relevant to the AIMS purpose and to achieving its intended results, incl. the organization's role(s) (provider, producer, user, etc.) and applicable AI-related climate/regulatory factors.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Include threat landscape/AI attack surface in context. (4.1)
items.Evidence to verify: Context analysis, AI role determination, issue register
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties
items.Requirement: Identify interested parties relevant to the AIMS, their requirements (incl. legal/regulatory, e.g. EU AI Act, PDPPL) and which will be addressed through the AIMS.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Security, privacy and regulatory requirements of stakeholders. (4.2)
items.Evidence to verify: Stakeholder register, AI regulatory/contractual requirements register
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Determining the scope of the AI management system
items.Requirement: Determine and document AIMS boundaries and applicability, considering 4.1, 4.2 and the AI systems in scope.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Scope should cover AI assets and their security boundaries. (4.3)
items.Evidence to verify: Approved AIMS scope statement, AI system list
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI management system
items.Requirement: Establish, implement, maintain and continually improve the AIMS, including needed processes and their interactions.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Integrate AIMS with the ISMS. (4.4)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Leadership and commitment
items.Requirement: Top management demonstrates commitment: AI policy and objectives aligned to strategy, AIMS integrated into processes, resources provided, importance of effective AI management communicated, outcomes ensured, improvement promoted.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Leadership commitment to security within AI governance. (5.1)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI policy
items.Requirement: Establish, document, communicate and make available an AI policy appropriate to the organization's purpose, providing a framework for AI objectives, committing to applicable requirements and continual improvement; consistent with other policies.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): AI policy must align with the information security policy. (5.2, A.5.1)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Roles, responsibilities and authorities
items.Requirement: Assign and communicate AIMS roles, incl. responsibility for conformity to the standard and reporting AIMS performance to top management.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Security roles for AI systems. (5.3, A.5.2)
items.Evidence to verify: RACI, AI governance charter, appointment records
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Actions to address risks and opportunities - General
items.Requirement: Determine risks and opportunities to give assurance the AIMS achieves outcomes, prevents/reduces undesired effects, and enables improvement; plan actions and evaluate effectiveness.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Security risks/opportunities feed AIMS planning. (6.1.1)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI system impact assessment
items.Requirement: Define a process to assess potential consequences of AI systems on individuals, groups and society through their life cycle; document and retain results.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Impacts from security failures (privacy breach, safety harm). (A.5.34)
items.Evidence to verify: Impact assessment procedure and completed assessments
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI objectives and planning to achieve them
items.Requirement: Establish measurable AI objectives at relevant functions/levels, consistent with the AI policy; plan what, resources, owner, deadline and evaluation.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Set security/robustness objectives for AI systems. (6.2)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Planning of changes
items.Requirement: Carry out AIMS changes in a planned manner when a need for change is determined.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Security review of AIMS/AI system changes. (6.3, A.8.32)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Resources
items.Requirement: Determine and provide resources needed to establish, implement, maintain and improve the AIMS.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Competence
items.Requirement: Determine necessary competence of persons affecting AI performance; ensure competence via education, training or experience; retain evidence.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): AI/ML security skills. (7.2, A.6.3)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Awareness
items.Requirement: Ensure persons are aware of the AI policy, their contribution to AIMS effectiveness and consequences of non-conformity.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Security awareness for AI users and developers. (7.3, A.6.3)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Communication
items.Requirement: Determine internal and external communications relevant to the AIMS: what, when, with whom, how.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Communication of security matters. (7.4)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Documented information - General
items.Requirement: AIMS includes documented information required by the standard and determined necessary for AIMS effectiveness.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Creating and updating documented information
items.Requirement: Ensure appropriate identification, description, format and review/approval.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Operational planning and control
items.Requirement: Plan, implement and control processes to meet requirements and execute 6.1 actions and 6.2 objectives; control planned changes, review unintended changes and control outsourced processes.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Operational security controls, incl. outsourced AI processes. (8.1, A.5.19)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI system impact assessment
items.Requirement: Perform AI system impact assessments per 6.1.4 at planned intervals or on significant change; retain results.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Reassess impacts after security or design changes. (A.5.34)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
items.Requirement: Determine what needs monitoring/measuring, methods, timing and responsibilities; evaluate AI performance and AIMS effectiveness; retain evidence.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Security monitoring/metrics for AI systems. (9.1, A.8.16)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Internal audit - General
items.Requirement: Conduct internal audits at planned intervals to check AIMS conformity to own requirements and the standard, and effective implementation.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Internal audit programme
items.Requirement: Plan programme (frequency, methods, responsibilities, reporting); define criteria/scope; select objective, impartial auditors; report to management; retain evidence.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items.Evidence to verify: Audit plan, auditor independence, findings log
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Management review - General
items.Requirement: Top management reviews the AIMS at planned intervals for continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Management review inputs
items.Requirement: Consider status of previous actions, changes in issues, AIMS performance (NCs, monitoring, audits, objectives), interested-party feedback, opportunities for improvement and risks.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Management review results
items.Requirement: Record decisions on continual improvement opportunities and any AIMS changes.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Continual improvement
items.Requirement: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the AIMS.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: Nonconformity and corrective action
items.Requirement: React to NCs, evaluate need to eliminate causes, implement and review corrective action effectiveness, update AIMS; retain evidence.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Corrective action after security incidents/NCs. (10.2, A.5.27)
items._section: Clauses 4-10

items.Title: AI policy
items.Requirement: Document a policy for the development or use of AI systems.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Reference security requirements in AI policy. (A.5.1)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Alignment with other organizational policies
items.Requirement: Determine where other policies (security, privacy, quality, safety, etc.) are affected by or apply to AI objectives, and align them.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Align with information security and privacy policies. (A.5.1)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Review of the AI policy
items.Requirement: Review the AI policy at planned intervals or on significant change to ensure continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: AI roles and responsibilities
items.Requirement: Define and allocate AI roles and responsibilities per organizational needs.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Security accountability for AI systems. (A.5.2, A.5.4)
items.Evidence to verify: AI governance roles, RACI, committee charter
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Reporting of concerns
items.Requirement: Define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization's role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Channel for security concerns. (A.6.8, A.5.26)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Resource documentation
items.Requirement: Identify and document relevant resources required for each AI system life-cycle stage and other AI-related activities, to understand and address risks/impacts.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Asset inventory of AI resources. (A.5.9)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Data resources
items.Requirement: Document information about data resources used for the AI system.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Classification and protection of datasets. (A.5.9, A.5.12)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Human resources
items.Requirement: Document human resources and their competences for development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning, and verification and integration of the AI system.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Vetted, trained AI personnel. (A.6.1, A.6.3)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: AI system impact assessment process
items.Requirement: Establish a process to assess potential consequences for individuals, groups and society from the AI system throughout its life cycle.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Include security and privacy harms in impact process. (A.5.34)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Documentation of AI system impact assessments
items.Requirement: Document results of impact assessments and retain for a defined period.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Assessing AI system impact on individuals or groups of individuals
items.Requirement: Assess and document impacts on individuals/groups throughout the life cycle (e.g. fairness, privacy, safety, rights).
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Privacy/safety impacts on individuals. (A.5.34)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Assessing societal impacts of AI systems
items.Requirement: Assess and document societal impacts (e.g. environment, economy, culture, public health, misinformation) throughout the life cycle.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Objectives for responsible development of AI system
items.Requirement: Identify and document objectives guiding responsible AI development (fairness, transparency, robustness, safety, etc.) and integrate them into the life cycle.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Robustness and security as responsible-AI objectives. (A.8.25)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Documentation of AI system design and development
items.Requirement: Document design and development per organizational objectives, documented requirements and criteria (architecture, model choices, training approach).
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Document secure architecture and design decisions. (A.8.27, A.5.37)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: AI system technical documentation
items.Requirement: Determine what AI system technical documentation is needed for each relevant category of interested parties and provide it.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Secure handling of technical documentation. (A.5.37, A.8.27)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Data for development and enhancement of AI system
items.Requirement: Define, document and implement data management processes related to AI development.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Data classification, masking, deletion. (A.5.12, A.8.10, A.8.11)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Acquisition of data
items.Requirement: Determine and document details about acquisition and selection of data used in AI systems.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Lawful, trusted data sources; supplier/data-broker risk. (A.5.19, A.5.34)
items.Evidence to verify: Data acquisition records, licences, consent basis
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Data preparation
items.Requirement: Define and document criteria for selecting data preparation methods and how they are used.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Protect sensitive data during preparation. (A.8.11, A.8.33, A.5.34)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: System documentation and information for users
items.Requirement: Determine and provide necessary information to users of the AI system.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Secure-use guidance for users. (A.5.37)
items.Evidence to verify: User guides, capability/limitation statements, transparency notices
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: External reporting
items.Requirement: Provide capability for interested parties to report adverse impacts of the AI system.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Channel to report security-relevant adverse impacts. (A.5.5, A.6.8)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Information for interested parties
items.Requirement: Determine and document obligations to report information about the AI system to interested parties.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Regulatory/contractual reporting obligations. (A.5.31, A.5.5)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Processes for responsible use of AI systems
items.Requirement: Define and document processes for responsible use of AI systems.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Acceptable use rules for AI. (A.5.10)
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Objectives for responsible use of AI system
items.Requirement: Identify and document objectives guiding responsible use, aligned to AI policy.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): None
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Intended use of the AI system
items.Requirement: Ensure the AI system is used according to its intended uses and accompanying documentation.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Prevent misuse via access control and monitoring. (A.5.10, A.8.16)
items.Evidence to verify: Use monitoring, misuse controls, user attestations
items._section: Annex A controls

items.Title: Customers
items.Requirement: Ensure the organization's responsible AI approach considers customer expectations and needs.
items.Security enabler link (indirect, if any): Customer security and data requirements. (A.5.20, A.5.34)
items._section: Annex A controls

headers: Security note / why CIA is involved

items.Title: Scope
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Operator (umbrella term covering Provider, Deployer, Importer, Distributor, Authorised Representative, Product Manufacturer) - this article determines which role(s) an organization holds and therefore which obligations apply.
items.Requirement: Determine applicability: providers, deployers, importers, distributors and product manufacturers placing AI systems/GPAI models on the EU market or whose output is used in the EU.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter I - General provisions

items.Title: Definitions
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: All roles - this article is the source of the role definitions themselves (see the Role Legend above).
items.Requirement: Apply the Act's definitions (AI system, provider, deployer, high-risk, GPAI model, serious incident, etc.) consistently across governance documents.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter I - General provisions

items.Title: AI literacy
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider and Deployer - both must ensure their own staff (and others acting on their behalf) have sufficient AI literacy.
items.Requirement: Take measures to ensure sufficient AI literacy of staff and others dealing with AI systems on the organization's behalf, considering their technical knowledge, experience and context of use.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter I - General provisions

items.Title: Prohibited AI practices
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider (must not place on market/put into service) and Deployer (must not use) - the prohibition binds both roles independently.
items.Requirement: Do not place on the market, put into service or use AI systems for prohibited practices: subliminal/manipulative techniques causing harm, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, real-time remote biometric ID in public for law enforcement (subject to exceptions), biometric categorisation inferring sensitive attributes, emotion recognition in workplace/education (with exceptions), untargeted facial-image scraping, individual crime-risk prediction based solely on profiling.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Emotion recognition, biometric categorisation and scraping controls overlap with data confidentiality and consent safeguards.
items._section: Chapter II - Prohibited AI practices

items.Title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - responsible for classifying their own AI system before placing it on the market or putting it into service.
items.Requirement: Determine whether an AI system is high-risk: safety component of a regulated product (Annex I) or use case listed in Annex III, with a narrow self-assessment exemption where risk is not significant.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S1 - High-risk classification

items.Title: Amendments to Annex III
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must monitor for classification-list changes affecting systems it has already placed on the market.
items.Requirement: Monitor Commission updates to the high-risk use-case list (Annex III) and re-assess systems accordingly.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S1 - High-risk classification

items.Title: Compliance with the requirements
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - primary and direct responsibility for meeting Articles 9-15 across the system's lifecycle.
items.Requirement: Ensure high-risk AI systems comply with Articles 9-15 throughout their lifecycle, considering intended purpose and generally acknowledged state of the art.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems

items.Title: Risk management system
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must establish and maintain the risk management system for the high-risk AI system.
items.Requirement: Establish, implement, document and maintain a continuous risk management process across the lifecycle: identify, analyse, estimate and evaluate known/foreseeable risks, adopt mitigation measures, and test.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Risk management must cover security/adversarial risks alongside safety and fundamental-rights risks.
items.Evidence to verify: AI risk management file, test reports
items._section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems

items.Title: Data and data governance
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - responsible for the data governance practices applied during development of the high-risk AI system.
items.Requirement: Apply data governance practices to training/validation/testing data: relevant design choices, provenance, collection, bias examination, gaps identification, and appropriate quality/representativeness; protect data appropriately.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Poor data governance is a direct integrity risk (poisoning, bias) and can expose confidential data if provenance/access is not controlled.
items._section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems

items.Title: Technical documentation
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must draw up and maintain the technical documentation per Annex IV.
items.Requirement: Draw up technical documentation before placing on the market/putting into service and keep it up to date, per Annex IV (system description, design, development, risk management, performance, changes).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems

items.Title: Record-keeping (logging)
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must design the logging capability into the system; Deployer - relies on and operates these logs during use (see Art.26).
items.Requirement: Design high-risk AI systems with capability for automatic logging of events over the system's lifetime to ensure traceability appropriate to intended purpose.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Tamper-evident, available logs are needed for traceability and incident investigation.
items.Evidence to verify: Logging design spec, log retention records
items._section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems

items.Title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must design for transparency and supply instructions for use; Deployer - is the recipient of this information and relies on it for compliant use.
items.Requirement: Design systems to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret output and use appropriately; provide instructions for use with required content (identity, characteristics, performance, known limitations, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems

items.Title: Human oversight
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must design the human-oversight interface/tools into the system; Deployer - must actually assign competent human oversight during use (see Art.26).
items.Requirement: Design high-risk AI systems, including appropriate human-machine interface tools, to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use, able to understand, monitor and intervene (incl. stop/override).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems

items.Title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - sole responsibility for designing and testing accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity into the system.
items.Requirement: Design and develop high-risk AI systems to achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, perform consistently, and be resilient to errors, faults, inconsistencies, and attempts by unauthorised third parties to exploit vulnerabilities (data poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion, confidentiality attacks), with technical redundancy/back-up where relevant.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Direct cybersecurity obligation: protect against attacks on confidentiality (model/data extraction), integrity (poisoning, adversarial manipulation) and availability (denial of service, faults).
items.Evidence to verify: Robustness/security test reports, resilience measures, cybersecurity controls
items._section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems

items.Title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - this article consolidates the full set of provider-specific obligations.
items.Requirement: Ensure conformity, have quality management system, keep documentation/logs, undergo conformity assessment, draw up EU declaration of conformity, affix CE marking, register system, take corrective action, cooperate with authorities.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Quality management system
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must establish and maintain the QMS.
items.Requirement: Put in place a quality management system documenting strategy for compliance, design control, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring, incident reporting, resource management, and an accountability framework.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Documentation keeping
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - the 10-year document retention duty rests with the provider.
items.Requirement: Keep technical documentation, QMS documentation, conformity assessment and EU declaration of conformity documentation for 10 years after placing on the market.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Automatically generated logs
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - retains logs that are under its control (contrast with Art.26, where the Deployer retains logs under its own control).
items.Requirement: Keep the logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system, to the extent they are under the provider's control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose (at least 6 months unless otherwise provided).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Preserving log integrity and availability for the retention period.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Corrective actions and duty of information
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must act and must notify Distributors, Deployers, the Authorised Representative and authorities as relevant.
items.Requirement: Take corrective actions or withdraw/recall a non-conforming system; inform distributors, deployers, authorised representative and, where relevant, authorities of the non-conformity and actions taken.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Cooperation with competent authorities
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - primary duty to cooperate; an Authorised Representative may also be approached where the provider is outside the EU.
items.Requirement: Provide competent authorities, on reasoned request, with information/documentation to demonstrate conformity, including access to automatically generated logs where relevant.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Ensure controlled, confidential handling of information shared with authorities.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Authorised representatives
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Authorised Representative - this article defines its role and mandated duties, appointed by a non-EU Provider.
items.Requirement: Non-EU providers appoint an EU authorised representative with a mandate covering conformity documentation, cooperation with authorities and registration duties.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Obligations of importers
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Importer - this article sets out the Importer's specific verification and cooperation duties.
items.Requirement: Verify conformity assessment, documentation and CE marking before placing a system on the market; ensure storage/transport conditions do not jeopardise compliance; cooperate with authorities.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Obligations of distributors
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Distributor - this article sets out the Distributor's specific verification duties.
items.Requirement: Verify CE marking, documentation and conformity before making a system available; not make available if non-conforming; take corrective action if aware of non-conformity.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Distributor, Importer, Deployer or third-party supplier - any of these can be re-classified as a Provider under the stated conditions and then assumes full Provider obligations.
items.Requirement: Determine when a distributor, importer, deployer or third party is considered a provider (e.g. substantial modification, own branding) and assumes provider obligations; third-party suppliers provide necessary information/access via written agreement.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Agreements should protect confidentiality of shared IP/technical information.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Deployer - this article consolidates the full set of deployer-specific obligations, the mirror of Art.16 for providers.
items.Requirement: Use systems per instructions, assign competent human oversight, ensure input data relevance, monitor operation, keep automatically generated logs (min. 6 months), inform provider/authorities of risks or serious incidents, cooperate with authorities, conduct data protection impact assessment where applicable.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Deployer must protect and retain logs and monitor for security-relevant anomalies.
items.Evidence to verify: Deployer operating procedures, log retention, DPIA
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Fundamental rights impact assessment
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Deployer - specifically deployers that are public bodies or private entities providing public services, or operating in banking/insurance, per the article's scope.
items.Requirement: Certain deployers (public bodies, banking/insurance, etc.) perform a fundamental rights impact assessment before deployment: process description, period/frequency of use, affected persons, specific risks, human oversight measures, and mitigation/governance measures.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III S3 - Provider/deployer obligations

items.Title: Obligations for providers of GPAI models
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: GPAI Model Provider - a provider specifically of a general-purpose AI model (distinct from, but can overlap with, a high-risk AI system Provider).
items.Requirement: Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, provide information/documentation to downstream providers, establish a copyright policy, publish a sufficiently detailed training-content summary.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: GPAI technical documentation, training data summary
items._section: Chapter V - General-purpose AI models

items.Title: Obligations for providers of GPAI models with systemic risk
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: GPAI Model Provider meeting the systemic-risk threshold (based on compute/capability criteria) - an elevated obligation tier on top of Art.53.
items.Requirement: Perform model evaluation incl. adversarial testing, assess and mitigate systemic risks, track/document/report serious incidents, ensure adequate cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Explicit cybersecurity protection obligation for the model and infrastructure against theft, unauthorized access and attacks.
items.Evidence to verify: Systemic risk assessment, adversarial test reports, incident log, cybersecurity measures
items._section: Chapter V - General-purpose AI models

items.Title: Transparency obligations for certain AI systems
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider (must design the disclosure/labelling capability into the system) and Deployer (must make the actual disclosure to natural persons at the point of interaction/use).
items.Requirement: Inform natural persons they are interacting with an AI system (unless obvious); mark synthetic audio/image/video/text (deepfakes) as AI-generated/manipulated; disclose AI-generated text on matters of public interest; disclose emotion-recognition/biometric-categorisation use to exposed persons.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter VIII - Transparency obligations

items.Title: Post-market monitoring by providers
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - must establish and operate the post-market monitoring system.
items.Requirement: Establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the AI technology and risks, actively/systematically collecting and analysing performance data throughout the system's lifetime.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Monitoring must detect performance degradation and security-relevant anomalies over time.
items._section: Chapter IX - Post-market monitoring and incident reporting

items.Title: Reporting of serious incidents
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - primary reporting duty; Deployer - must also inform the Provider (or importer/distributor) and relevant authorities of any serious incident it identifies (per Art.26).
items.Requirement: Report serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems to market surveillance authorities without undue delay (specified timelines, incl. immediate for widespread infringement/critical infrastructure), investigate and take corrective action.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Security incidents affecting the AI system fall within serious-incident reporting duties.
items._section: Chapter IX - Post-market monitoring and incident reporting

items.Title: Penalties
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: All roles (Provider, Deployer, Importer, Distributor, Authorised Representative, GPAI Provider) - penalties apply to whichever role is found non-compliant with its specific obligations.
items.Requirement: Ensure compliance to avoid administrative fines (tiered by severity, up to the higher of EUR 35m or 7% of global turnover for prohibited-practice breaches).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter XII - Penalties

items.Title: High-risk AI system use cases
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - uses this annex to classify its system (Art.6); Deployer - should also be aware of it, particularly public-sector and essential-services deployers subject to Art.27 FRIA.
items.Requirement: Check whether the AI system falls under a listed high-risk use case (biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services incl. access to insurance/credit, law enforcement, migration/asylum/border, justice/democratic processes).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter XII - Penalties

items.Title: Technical documentation content
items.Applicable Role(s) & Responsibilities: Provider - sole responsibility for producing technical documentation to this content standard (Art.11).
items.Requirement: Ensure technical documentation covers general description, design/development process and choices, monitoring/functioning/control, risk management measures, lifecycle changes, standards applied, and EU declaration of conformity.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter XII - Penalties

headers: Security note / why CIA is involved

items.Title: Inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being
items.Requirement: AI actors should proactively engage in responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI for beneficial outcomes: augmenting human capabilities, advancing inclusion of underrepresented populations, reducing inequalities, and protecting the environment.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 1 - Values-based principles for trustworthy AI

items.Title: Human rights, democratic values and fairness (incl. privacy)
items.Requirement: Respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic values throughout the AI system lifecycle: non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and labour rights; implement mechanisms such as human oversight where needed.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Privacy and data protection require confidentiality controls over personal data used by AI systems.
items.Evidence to verify: Fairness/bias testing, privacy impact assessment, human oversight design
items._section: Section 1 - Values-based principles for trustworthy AI

items.Title: Transparency and explainability
items.Requirement: AI actors should provide meaningful information appropriate to context: to foster understanding, inform of AI interaction, enable those affected to understand outcomes, and enable those adversely affected to challenge outcomes based on plain and easy-to-understand information on factors and logic.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 1 - Values-based principles for trustworthy AI

items.Title: Robustness, security and safety
items.Requirement: AI systems should function appropriately and not pose unreasonable safety/security risks throughout their lifecycle; traceability of datasets, processes and decisions; risk-based approach with continuous risk management (security, safety, bias) applied by AI actors to each phase; safeguards to ensure control can be reasserted (e.g. deactivation) when risks materialize.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Directly requires security throughout the lifecycle: resilience against attacks, traceability (integrity), safe operation (availability/safety) and the ability to disable a malfunctioning or compromised system.
items.Evidence to verify: Robustness/security testing, risk management process, traceability records, deactivation/kill-switch controls
items._section: Section 1 - Values-based principles for trustworthy AI

items.Title: Accountability
items.Requirement: AI actors should be accountable for the proper functioning of AI systems and respect of the principles, based on their roles, context, and consistent with the state of the art; enable traceability, incl. logging, to analyse outcomes and responses to inquiry; apply a systematic risk management approach to each phase of the lifecycle on an ongoing basis.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Traceability/logging for accountability protects integrity of the record and requires availability of logs for inquiry.
items.Evidence to verify: Accountability framework, role assignment, logging and audit trail
items._section: Section 1 - Values-based principles for trustworthy AI

items.Title: Investing in AI research and development
items.Requirement: Foster investment in R&D, incl. long-term public investment and encouragement of private investment, to spur innovation in trustworthy AI.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 2 - Policy recommendations for governments (organizational relevance)

items.Title: Fostering an inclusive AI-enabling ecosystem
items.Requirement: Foster accessible AI ecosystems with digital infrastructure, technologies, mechanisms to share data and knowledge responsibly and share metrics to measure AI research/development/deployment/growth.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 2 - Policy recommendations for governments (organizational relevance)

items.Title: Shaping an enabling interoperable governance and policy environment
items.Requirement: Promote a policy environment that supports agile transition from R&D to deployment, incl. mechanisms such as regulatory sandboxes to experiment with AI safely, and work towards interoperable governance frameworks.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 2 - Policy recommendations for governments (organizational relevance)

items.Title: Building human capacity and preparing for labour-market transformation
items.Requirement: Equip people with skills for AI, support workers in transitioning jobs affected by AI, and ensure protection of labour rights.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 2 - Policy recommendations for governments (organizational relevance)

items.Title: International co-operation for trustworthy AI
items.Requirement: Actively co-operate across borders and sectors to advance responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI, incl. common understanding of AI actor obligations, interoperable governance, standards and metrics.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items.Evidence to verify: Participation in international AI governance initiatives
items._section: Section 2 - Policy recommendations for governments (organizational relevance)

items.Title: General-purpose and generative AI risks
items.Requirement: Address risks specific to general-purpose/foundation and generative AI models, incl. safety, misuse and information-integrity risks (e.g. disinformation, deepfakes).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 3 - 2024 update focus areas

items.Title: Environmental footprint
items.Requirement: Consider and where possible measure/reduce the environmental footprint (energy, compute, resources) of AI systems across their lifecycle.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 3 - 2024 update focus areas

items.Title: Intellectual property rights
items.Requirement: Respect intellectual property rights, incl. in relation to training data and generated content.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 3 - 2024 update focus areas

items.Title: Multi-stakeholder co-operation on risk
items.Requirement: Engage multiple stakeholders (government, industry, civil society, academia, technical community) to manage AI risks and information integrity collaboratively.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/policy-level recommendation.
items._section: Section 3 - 2024 update focus areas

headers: Security note / why CIA is involved

items.Category outcome: Policies, processes, procedures and practices for mapping, measuring and managing AI risk are established, documented and effectively implemented, reflecting organizational risk tolerance.
items.Suggested action: Establish AI risk-management policies/processes covering legal/regulatory requirements, and review/update them regularly.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items.Evidence to verify: AI risk management policy, process documentation, review log
items._section: GOVERN - GOVERN - policy, accountability and culture (cross-cutting; applies to the whole organization)

items.Category outcome: Accountability structures are in place so appropriate teams and individuals are empowered, responsible and trained for mapping, measuring and managing AI risks.
items.Suggested action: Assign clear roles/responsibilities for AI risk management and provide training.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: GOVERN - GOVERN - policy, accountability and culture (cross-cutting; applies to the whole organization)

items.Category outcome: Workforce diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility processes are prioritized, and organizational risk management supported by a diverse team.
items.Suggested action: Ensure diverse, multidisciplinary teams involved in AI risk decisions.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: GOVERN - GOVERN - policy, accountability and culture (cross-cutting; applies to the whole organization)

items.Category outcome: Organizational teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk.
items.Suggested action: Foster risk-aware culture, incl. incentives, policies for documenting risks/tradeoffs, and processes for flagging risks.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: GOVERN - GOVERN - policy, accountability and culture (cross-cutting; applies to the whole organization)

items.Category outcome: Processes are in place for robust engagement with relevant AI actors (incl. external stakeholders and end users).
items.Suggested action: Establish mechanisms to solicit and incorporate feedback from relevant AI actors.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: GOVERN - GOVERN - policy, accountability and culture (cross-cutting; applies to the whole organization)

items.Category outcome: Policies and procedures are in place to address AI risks and benefits arising from third-party software/data/systems and other supply-chain issues.
items.Suggested action: Establish third-party/AI supply-chain risk management processes, incl. contracts and due diligence.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Third-party/supply-chain AI components (models, data, libraries) are a confidentiality risk vector requiring security due diligence, similar to ISO 27001 supplier controls.
items.Evidence to verify: Third-party AI risk policy, vendor due-diligence records, contract clauses
items._section: GOVERN - GOVERN - policy, accountability and culture (cross-cutting; applies to the whole organization)

items.Category outcome: Context is established and understood: intended purpose, business value, risk tolerances, requirements, and impacted stakeholders identified.
items.Suggested action: Document AI system context: purpose, users, requirements (incl. legal/regulatory and security requirements).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: MAP - MAP - context, categorization and impacts (system-level)

items.Category outcome: Categorization of the AI system is performed, incl. specific tasks and methods used to implement them.
items.Suggested action: Categorize the AI system by task, method (e.g. classification, generative), and risk level.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: MAP - MAP - context, categorization and impacts (system-level)

items.Category outcome: AI capabilities, targeted usage, goals and expected benefits/costs are understood compared with appropriate benchmarks.
items.Suggested action: Document expected AI system performance and benchmarks; consider failure/edge cases.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: MAP - MAP - context, categorization and impacts (system-level)

items.Category outcome: Risks and benefits are mapped for all components of the AI system, incl. third-party software, data and other supply-chain elements.
items.Suggested action: Identify and document risks/benefits of each AI system component, incl. third-party/open-source elements.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Mapping risks of models/data/components from the supply chain is core to protecting confidentiality, integrity and availability of the system.
items._section: MAP - MAP - context, categorization and impacts (system-level)

items.Category outcome: Impacts to individuals, groups, communities, organizations and society are characterized/understood.
items.Suggested action: Assess likelihood and magnitude of impacts, incl. via consultation with affected communities where relevant.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: MAP - MAP - context, categorization and impacts (system-level)

items.Category outcome: Appropriate methods and metrics are identified and applied to AI risks, and effectiveness of metrics evaluated.
items.Suggested action: Select and document metrics for measuring AI risks (performance, fairness, robustness, etc.).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: MEASURE - MEASURE - testing, evaluation and monitoring (system-level)

items.Category outcome: AI systems are evaluated for trustworthy characteristics: valid/reliable, safe, secure/resilient, accountable/transparent, explainable/interpretable, privacy-enhanced, fair with harmful bias managed.
items.Suggested action: Test and document evaluation of each trustworthy characteristic, incl. security and resilience testing against adversarial/abuse scenarios.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: 'Secure and resilient' is an explicit trustworthy characteristic requiring testing against attacks, unauthorized access and manipulation - directly CIA.
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports covering security/resilience, robustness, bias, privacy
items._section: MEASURE - MEASURE - testing, evaluation and monitoring (system-level)

items.Category outcome: Mechanisms for tracking identified AI risks over time are in place.
items.Suggested action: Implement ongoing monitoring/tracking of identified risks (incl. security incidents, drift, anomalies) with regular review.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Continuous monitoring must detect security-relevant drift, anomalies and incidents to preserve integrity and availability.
items.Evidence to verify: Risk tracking log, monitoring dashboards, incident tracking
items._section: MEASURE - MEASURE - testing, evaluation and monitoring (system-level)

items.Category outcome: Feedback about efficacy of measurement is gathered and assessed.
items.Suggested action: Gather feedback (incl. from red-teaming, external audits, user reports) and use it to improve measurement approaches.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: MEASURE - MEASURE - testing, evaluation and monitoring (system-level)

items.Category outcome: AI risks based on assessments from the Map and Measure functions are prioritized, responded to and managed.
items.Suggested action: Prioritize and treat AI risks per organizational risk tolerance; document risk response decisions.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: MANAGE - MANAGE - risk prioritization, treatment and response (system-level)

items.Category outcome: Strategies to maximize AI benefits and minimize negative impacts are planned, prepared, implemented, documented and informed by input from relevant AI actors.
items.Suggested action: Implement mitigation strategies and periodically reassess effectiveness.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - governance/process-level outcome.
items._section: MANAGE - MANAGE - risk prioritization, treatment and response (system-level)

items.Category outcome: AI risks and benefits from third-party entities are managed.
items.Suggested action: Monitor and manage risks from third-party AI systems/components throughout their lifecycle, incl. contractual and technical controls.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Managing security risk from third-party AI systems/components on an ongoing basis (patches, vulnerabilities, access).
items.Evidence to verify: Third-party risk register, ongoing supplier monitoring
items._section: MANAGE - MANAGE - risk prioritization, treatment and response (system-level)

items.Category outcome: Risk treatments, incl. response and recovery, and communication plans for the identified and measured AI risks are documented and monitored regularly.
items.Suggested action: Establish and test incident response/recovery plans for AI-related incidents; maintain communication plans for affected stakeholders and authorities.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Incident response and recovery for AI systems directly protects confidentiality, integrity and availability when things go wrong.
items.Evidence to verify: AI incident response/recovery plan, communication plan, test/exercise records
items._section: MANAGE - MANAGE - risk prioritization, treatment and response (system-level)

headers: Security note / why CIA is involved

items.Title: Terms, definitions and overview of AI system impact assessment (AISIA)
items.Guidance point: Adopt the standard's terminology (AI system impact assessment, affected stakeholder, AI actor, etc.) and understand its purpose: assessing how an AI system and its foreseeable applications may affect individuals, groups and society across the lifecycle.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 4 - General / terms and definitions

items.Title: Purpose and scope of the AISIA process
items.Guidance point: Establish why and for which AI systems/use cases the organization will perform impact assessments, and how the process applies across sizes/types of organization.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Roles and responsibilities
items.Guidance point: Assign roles for conducting, reviewing and approving impact assessments (e.g. assessors, AI system owner, independent reviewer, affected-party liaison).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Triggers and timing across the AI system lifecycle
items.Guidance point: Determine when an AISIA is performed or updated: initial design, before deployment, on significant change, periodically in operation, and at decommissioning.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items.Evidence to verify: AISIA trigger criteria, lifecycle checkpoint schedule
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Planning the assessment
items.Guidance point: Plan scope, resources, timeline, methodology and tools for each AISIA, proportionate to the AI system's risk and context.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Understanding context and intended/foreseeable use
items.Guidance point: Gather information on the AI system's purpose, intended use, reasonably foreseeable misuse, deployment context and data used.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Identifying affected stakeholders
items.Guidance point: Identify individuals, groups, communities and society that could be affected by the AI system, directly or indirectly.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Identifying potential impacts
items.Guidance point: Identify potential positive and negative impacts (e.g. on rights, safety, fairness, autonomy, economic, environmental, security-related harms) arising from intended and foreseeable use.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Identification should include impacts from security failures (e.g. unauthorized disclosure or manipulation of personal data) alongside ethical/societal harms.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Analysing and evaluating impacts
items.Guidance point: Analyse likelihood and severity of identified impacts, and evaluate them against organizational risk criteria and stakeholder expectations.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Determining and implementing mitigation actions
items.Guidance point: Identify options to prevent, reduce or otherwise address negative impacts, decide and implement appropriate actions, and record residual impact.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items.Evidence to verify: Mitigation action plan, residual impact sign-off
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Review, monitoring and reassessment
items.Guidance point: Monitor the AI system and its context for change, and review/update the impact assessment periodically or when triggers in 5.3 occur.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: Integration with AI risk management and the AI management system
items.Guidance point: Integrate AISIA outputs into the organization's AI risk assessment/treatment process and AI management system (e.g. ISO/IEC 42001 clauses 6.1.2 and 6.1.4).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 5 - Developing and implementing an AI system impact assessment (AISIA) process

items.Title: General documentation requirements
items.Guidance point: Determine what information must be documented for each AISIA to support transparency, accountability and traceability of the process and its outcomes.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 6 - Documenting the AI system impact assessment

items.Title: Content of the impact assessment record
items.Guidance point: Document scope, context, affected stakeholders, identified impacts, analysis/evaluation, decisions, mitigation actions and residual impacts, and who approved the assessment.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Clause 6 - Documenting the AI system impact assessment

items.Title: Retention, version control and integrity of records
items.Guidance point: Maintain AISIA documentation over time, with version control, so records remain accurate, traceable and available for the required retention period.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Impact-assessment records must retain integrity and be protected from unauthorized alteration to remain a trustworthy audit trail.
items._section: Clause 6 - Documenting the AI system impact assessment

items.Title: Communication of results
items.Guidance point: Determine what impact assessment information is communicated to interested parties (e.g. management, regulators, affected stakeholders) and how.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items.Evidence to verify: Communication plan/records, published summaries where applicable
items._section: Clause 6 - Documenting the AI system impact assessment

items.Title: Confidentiality and access control of assessment records
items.Guidance point: Control access to AISIA documentation appropriately, since records may contain sensitive information about individuals, vulnerabilities or system design.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Impact assessment records can reveal personal data, vulnerabilities or system weaknesses and need confidentiality protection.
items._section: Clause 6 - Documenting the AI system impact assessment

items.Title: Guidance for use with ISO/IEC 42001
items.Guidance point: Use this annex to align the AISIA process with the AI management system requirements of ISO/IEC 42001, incl. clauses 6.1.2 (AI risk assessment), 6.1.4 (AI system impact assessment) and Annex A.5 controls.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items.Evidence to verify: Cross-reference to ISO 42001 6.1.2/6.1.4/A.5 items in this workbook

items.Title: Guidance for use with ISO/IEC 23894
items.Guidance point: Use this annex to align the AISIA process with AI risk management guidance in ISO/IEC 23894 (built on ISO 31000).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items.Evidence to verify: Cross-reference to AI risk management process
items._section: Annexes - Informative annexes

items.Title: Example impact categories and considerations
items.Guidance point: Consider the standard's example impact categories (e.g. individual, group, societal, environmental) and illustrative considerations when identifying impacts in 5.7.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items.Evidence to verify: Impact category checklist used in assessments
items._section: Annexes - Informative annexes

items.Title: AI system impact assessment template
items.Guidance point: Use or adapt the standard's AISIA template to structure and document individual assessments consistently across the organization.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - ethical/societal/governance guidance point.
items._section: Annexes - Informative annexes

items.Title: Understanding the organization and its context
items.Security requirement: Determine external/internal issues relevant to ISMS purpose and intended outcomes.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 4 - Context of the organization

items.Title: Understanding needs and expectations of interested parties
items.Security requirement: Identify interested parties, their ISMS-relevant requirements (legal, regulatory, contractual) and which are addressed by the ISMS.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Interested-parties register, legal/regulatory register (e.g. PDPPL, QCB/CRA)
items._section: 4 - Context of the organization

items.Title: Determining the scope of the ISMS
items.Security requirement: Define and document ISMS boundaries and applicability, considering 4.1, 4.2 and interfaces/dependencies.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 4 - Context of the organization

items.Title: Information security management system
items.Security requirement: Establish, implement, maintain and continually improve the ISMS, including needed processes and interactions.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 4 - Context of the organization

items.Title: Leadership and commitment
items.Security requirement: Top management demonstrates commitment: policy/objectives aligned to strategy, ISMS integrated in processes, resources provided, importance communicated, outcomes ensured, improvement promoted.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Management minutes, budget approvals, sponsor communications
items._section: 5 - Leadership

items.Title: Policy
items.Security requirement: Establish an information security policy suited to the purpose, providing objectives/framework, commitment to requirements and continual improvement; documented, communicated, available to interested parties.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 5 - Leadership

items.Title: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
items.Security requirement: Assign and communicate ISMS roles, incl. responsibility for conformity and for reporting performance to top management.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 5 - Leadership

items.Title: Actions to address risks and opportunities - General
items.Security requirement: Plan actions for risks/opportunities from 4.1 and 4.2 so ISMS achieves outcomes, prevents undesired effects and improves; integrate and evaluate effectiveness.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 6 - Planning

items.Title: Information security risk assessment
items.Security requirement: Define and apply a risk assessment process: risk criteria, repeatable/comparable results, identify risks and owners, analyse likelihood/consequence, evaluate against criteria; retain documented information.
items.Why CIA is involved: Security risk assessment process covering confidentiality, integrity and availability risks.
items.Evidence to verify: Risk methodology, risk register, risk assessment reports
items._section: 6 - Planning

items.Title: Information security risk treatment
items.Security requirement: Select treatment options; determine all necessary controls (compare against Annex A); produce Statement of Applicability with justification for inclusions/exclusions; formulate treatment plan; obtain risk owner approval of plan and residual risk.
items.Why CIA is involved: Selects and treats security risks/controls across CIA.
items.Evidence to verify: Risk treatment plan, SoA, residual risk acceptance
items._section: 6 - Planning

items.Title: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them
items.Security requirement: Set measurable, monitored, communicated objectives consistent with policy; plan what, resources, owner, deadline, evaluation.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 6 - Planning

items.Title: Planning of changes
items.Security requirement: Carry out ISMS changes (identified as needed) in a planned manner.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Change records for ISMS, impact assessments
items._section: 6 - Planning

items.Title: Resources
items.Security requirement: Determine and provide resources needed for establishing, implementing, maintaining and improving the ISMS.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 7 - Support

items.Title: Competence
items.Security requirement: Determine necessary competence of persons affecting security performance; ensure competence via education/training/experience; take actions and retain evidence.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 7 - Support

items.Title: Awareness
items.Security requirement: Ensure persons are aware of policy, their contribution to ISMS effectiveness and implications of non-conformity.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 7 - Support

items.Title: Communication
items.Security requirement: Determine internal/external ISMS communications: what, when, with whom, who communicates, and process.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 7 - Support

items.Title: Documented information - General
items.Security requirement: ISMS includes documented information required by the standard and determined necessary for effectiveness.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 7 - Support

items.Title: Creating and updating
items.Security requirement: Ensure appropriate identification/description, format/media, review and approval.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 7 - Support

items.Title: Control of documented information
items.Security requirement: Control availability, protection, distribution, access, storage, version control, retention/disposition; control external-origin documents.
items.Why CIA is involved: Protecting documented information from unauthorized access and alteration.
items.Evidence to verify: DMS configuration, access and retention rules
items._section: 7 - Support

items.Title: Operational planning and control
items.Security requirement: Plan, implement and control processes to meet requirements and 6.1 actions; set criteria; keep documented information; control planned changes and outsourced processes.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 8 - Operation

items.Title: Information security risk assessment
items.Security requirement: Perform risk assessments at planned intervals or on significant change; retain results.
items.Why CIA is involved: Operational security risk assessment.
items._section: 8 - Operation

items.Title: Information security risk treatment
items.Security requirement: Implement the risk treatment plan; retain results of treatment.
items.Why CIA is involved: Operational implementation of security risk treatment.
items._section: 8 - Operation

items.Title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
items.Security requirement: Determine what to monitor/measure, methods, when, who; evaluate security performance and ISMS effectiveness; retain evidence.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 9 - Performance evaluation

items.Title: Internal audit - General
items.Security requirement: Conduct internal audits at planned intervals to check conformity to own requirements and the standard, and effective implementation.
