items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 9 - Performance evaluation

items.Title: Internal audit programme
items.Security requirement: Plan programme (frequency, methods, responsibilities, reporting); define criteria/scope; select objective, impartial auditors; report to management; retain evidence.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Audit plan, auditor independence records, findings log
items._section: 9 - Performance evaluation

items.Title: Management review - General
items.Security requirement: Top management reviews the ISMS at planned intervals for suitability, adequacy, effectiveness.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 9 - Performance evaluation

items.Title: Management review inputs
items.Security requirement: Consider status of previous actions, changes in issues, feedback on performance (NCs, monitoring, audits, objectives), interested-party feedback, risk assessment/treatment status, improvement opportunities.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 9 - Performance evaluation

items.Title: Management review results
items.Security requirement: Record decisions on improvement opportunities and any ISMS changes; retain as documented information.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 9 - Performance evaluation

items.Title: Continual improvement
items.Security requirement: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the ISMS.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 10 - Improvement

items.Title: Nonconformity and corrective action
items.Security requirement: React to NCs, evaluate need to eliminate causes, implement and review corrective action for effectiveness, update ISMS; retain evidence.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: 10 - Improvement

items.Title: Policies for information security
items.Security requirement: Define, approve, publish, communicate and review the information security policy and topic-specific policies at planned intervals.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Information security roles and responsibilities
items.Security requirement: Define and allocate security roles per organizational needs.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Segregation of duties
items.Security requirement: Segregate conflicting duties and areas of responsibility.
items.Why CIA is involved: Segregation of duties reduces risk of undetected fraud/error affecting integrity.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Management responsibilities
items.Security requirement: Management requires all personnel to apply security per policies and procedures.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Contact with authorities
items.Security requirement: Maintain contact with relevant authorities (e.g. regulator, CERT, law enforcement).
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Contact with special interest groups
items.Security requirement: Maintain contact with security forums and professional associations.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Threat intelligence
items.Security requirement: Collect and analyse information on threats to produce threat intelligence.
items.Why CIA is involved: Threat intelligence informs defenses across confidentiality, integrity and availability.
items.Evidence to verify: TI sources, TI reports, use in risk/detection
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Information security in project management
items.Security requirement: Integrate security into project management across all projects.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
items.Security requirement: Develop and maintain inventory of information and associated assets with owners.
items.Why CIA is involved: Asset inventory is foundational to knowing what needs protecting.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
items.Security requirement: Identify, document and implement rules for acceptable use and handling.
items.Why CIA is involved: Acceptable use limits misuse that could expose information.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Return of assets
items.Security requirement: Personnel and other parties return all assets on change or termination.
items.Why CIA is involved: Ensures assets/data are not retained inappropriately after use.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Classification of information
items.Security requirement: Classify information by confidentiality, integrity, availability and interested-party requirements.
items.Why CIA is involved: Classification underpins confidentiality protection.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Labelling of information
items.Security requirement: Develop and implement labelling procedures per classification scheme.
items.Why CIA is involved: Labelling supports correct handling per confidentiality level.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Information transfer
items.Security requirement: Establish transfer rules, procedures or agreements for all transfer facilities.
items.Why CIA is involved: Transfer controls protect data in transit.
items.Evidence to verify: Transfer policy, NDAs/agreements, secure transfer tools
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Access control
items.Security requirement: Establish and implement rules to control physical and logical access based on business and security requirements.
items.Why CIA is involved: Core access control protecting all three properties.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Identity management
items.Security requirement: Manage the full life cycle of identities.
items.Why CIA is involved: Identity lifecycle management underpins access security.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Authentication information
items.Security requirement: Control allocation and management of authentication information incl. user guidance.
items.Why CIA is involved: Authentication information protects access to systems.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Access rights
items.Security requirement: Provision, review, modify and remove access rights per policy.
items.Why CIA is involved: Access rights management controls who can reach what.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Information security in supplier relationships
items.Security requirement: Define and implement processes to manage supplier-related security risks.
items.Why CIA is involved: Supplier risk affects confidentiality, integrity and availability of shared assets.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
items.Security requirement: Establish and agree relevant security requirements with each supplier.
items.Why CIA is involved: Contractual security requirements with suppliers.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
items.Security requirement: Manage security risks in ICT products/services supply chain.
items.Why CIA is involved: ICT supply chain risk (compromised components/software).
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
items.Security requirement: Regularly monitor, review, evaluate and manage change in supplier practices and service delivery.
items.Why CIA is involved: Ongoing supplier monitoring for security posture.
items.Evidence to verify: Supplier reviews, SLA/security reports, audit rights
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Information security for use of cloud services
items.Security requirement: Establish processes for acquisition, use, management and exit of cloud services.
items.Why CIA is involved: Cloud security spans all three properties.
items.Evidence to verify: Cloud policy, shared-responsibility matrix, exit plan
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
items.Security requirement: Plan and prepare incident management: processes, roles, responsibilities.
items.Why CIA is involved: Incident planning underpins ability to protect CIA when incidents occur.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Assessment and decision on information security events
items.Security requirement: Assess events and decide whether to classify as incidents.
items.Why CIA is involved: Assessing events to determine CIA impact.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Response to information security incidents
items.Security requirement: Respond to incidents per documented procedures.
items.Why CIA is involved: Responding to incidents restores CIA.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Learning from information security incidents
items.Security requirement: Use knowledge from incidents to strengthen controls.
items.Why CIA is involved: Lessons learned improve control integrity/effectiveness.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Collection of evidence
items.Security requirement: Establish procedures for identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of evidence.
items.Why CIA is involved: Evidence collection preserves integrity for investigations.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Information security during disruption
items.Security requirement: Plan how to maintain security at an appropriate level during disruption.
items.Why CIA is involved: Maintaining security during disruption protects availability.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: ICT readiness for business continuity
items.Security requirement: Plan, implement, maintain and test ICT readiness based on BC objectives and ICT continuity requirements.
items.Why CIA is involved: ICT continuity protects availability.
items.Evidence to verify: BIA, DR plans, DR test results (RTO/RPO)
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
items.Security requirement: Identify, document and keep current legal/regulatory/contractual requirements and how they are met.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Intellectual property rights
items.Security requirement: Implement procedures to protect intellectual property rights.
items.Why CIA is involved: Protects confidentiality of licensed/IP material.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Protection of records
items.Security requirement: Protect records from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access and release.
items.Why CIA is involved: Protects records from loss, falsification or unauthorized release.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Privacy and protection of PII
items.Security requirement: Identify and meet requirements for privacy and PII protection per law and contract.
items.Why CIA is involved: Protects confidentiality of personal data.
items.Evidence to verify: Privacy policy, ROPA, DPIAs, DSAR process
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Independent review of information security
items.Security requirement: Review the organization's security approach independently at planned intervals and on significant change.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
items.Security requirement: Regularly review compliance with policies, topic-specific policies, rules and standards.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Documented operating procedures
items.Security requirement: Document operating procedures and make available to personnel who need them.
items.Why CIA is involved: Documented procedures support consistent, correct (integrity) operations.
items._section: A.5 - Organizational controls

items.Title: Screening
items.Security requirement: Verify candidates' background before joining and on an ongoing basis per laws and risk.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.6 - People controls

items.Title: Terms and conditions of employment
items.Security requirement: Employment agreements state personnel and organizational security responsibilities.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.6 - People controls

items.Title: Information security awareness, education and training
items.Security requirement: Provide appropriate awareness, education, training and regular policy updates.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.6 - People controls

items.Title: Disciplinary process
items.Security requirement: Formalize and communicate a disciplinary process for security policy violations.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: A.6 - People controls

items.Title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
items.Security requirement: Define, enforce and communicate security duties that remain valid after termination/change.
items.Why CIA is involved: Post-employment confidentiality obligations continue.
items._section: A.6 - People controls

items.Title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
items.Security requirement: Identify, document, review and sign NDAs reflecting protection needs.
items.Why CIA is involved: NDAs protect confidentiality of shared information.
items._section: A.6 - People controls

items.Title: Remote working
items.Security requirement: Implement security measures when personnel work remotely.
items.Why CIA is involved: Remote working introduces risk across all three properties.
items._section: A.6 - People controls

items.Title: Information security event reporting
items.Security requirement: Provide a mechanism for personnel to report observed/suspected events promptly.
items.Why CIA is involved: Timely event reporting preserves integrity of response.
items._section: A.6 - People controls

items.Title: Physical security perimeters
items.Security requirement: Define and use security perimeters to protect areas with information and assets.
items.Why CIA is involved: Perimeters protect against unauthorized physical access and disruption.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Physical entry
items.Security requirement: Protect secure areas with entry controls and access points.
items.Why CIA is involved: Entry controls limit unauthorized physical access.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
items.Security requirement: Design and implement physical security for offices, rooms and facilities.
items.Why CIA is involved: Facility security protects assets housed within.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Physical security monitoring
items.Security requirement: Continuously monitor premises for unauthorized physical access.
items.Why CIA is involved: Monitoring detects unauthorized physical access.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
items.Security requirement: Design and implement protection against fire, flood, and other natural or man-made threats.
items.Why CIA is involved: Protects against environmental threats to availability.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Working in secure areas
items.Security requirement: Design and implement security measures for working in secure areas.
items.Why CIA is involved: Secure-area working rules protect confidentiality.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Clear desk and clear screen
items.Security requirement: Define and enforce clear desk (papers/media) and clear screen rules.
items.Why CIA is involved: Clear desk/screen reduces exposure of sensitive information.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Equipment siting and protection
items.Security requirement: Site and protect equipment to reduce environmental risks and unauthorized access.
items.Why CIA is involved: Equipment siting reduces environmental and access risk.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Security of assets off-premises
items.Security requirement: Protect off-site assets.
items.Why CIA is involved: Protects assets used outside the office.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Storage media
items.Security requirement: Manage storage media through acquisition, use, transport and disposal per classification.
items.Why CIA is involved: Media handling protects data confidentiality and integrity.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Supporting utilities
items.Security requirement: Protect facilities from power failures and other utility disruptions.
items.Why CIA is involved: Utilities support availability of processing facilities.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Cabling security
items.Security requirement: Protect power/data/service cabling from interception, interference or damage.
items.Why CIA is involved: Cabling protection prevents interception/damage.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Equipment maintenance
items.Security requirement: Maintain equipment correctly to ensure availability, integrity and confidentiality.
items.Why CIA is involved: Maintenance sustains availability and reliability.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
items.Security requirement: Verify data and licensed software are removed/overwritten before disposal or re-use.
items.Why CIA is involved: Secure disposal prevents data leakage from decommissioned equipment.
items._section: A.7 - Physical controls

items.Title: User endpoint devices
items.Security requirement: Protect information stored on, processed by or accessible via user endpoints.
items.Why CIA is involved: Endpoint protection spans all three properties.
items.Evidence to verify: EDR, MDM, disk encryption, hardening baseline
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Privileged access rights
items.Security requirement: Restrict and manage allocation and use of privileged access rights.
items.Why CIA is involved: Privileged access is a high-impact CIA control.
items.Evidence to verify: PAM (e.g. CyberArk) records, privileged access reviews
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Information access restriction
items.Security requirement: Restrict access to information and assets per access control policy.
items.Why CIA is involved: Restricting access protects confidentiality.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Access to source code
items.Security requirement: Appropriately manage read/write access to source code, dev tools and libraries.
items.Why CIA is involved: Source code access control protects confidentiality and integrity of code.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Secure authentication
items.Security requirement: Implement secure authentication technologies and procedures based on access restrictions.
items.Why CIA is involved: Authentication underpins secure access.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Capacity management
items.Security requirement: Monitor and adjust resource use against capacity requirements.
items.Why CIA is involved: Capacity management supports availability.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Protection against malware
items.Security requirement: Implement malware protection supported by user awareness.
items.Why CIA is involved: Malware protection preserves integrity and availability.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
items.Security requirement: Obtain vulnerability info, assess exposure and take appropriate measures.
items.Why CIA is involved: Vulnerability management reduces exposure across all properties.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Configuration management
items.Security requirement: Establish, document, implement, monitor and review configurations incl. security configurations.
items.Why CIA is involved: Configuration management maintains secure, consistent state.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Information deletion
items.Security requirement: Delete information in systems, devices or media when no longer required.
items.Why CIA is involved: Deletion prevents unauthorized retention/exposure of data.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Data masking
items.Security requirement: Use data masking per access control and business requirements, incl. legal requirements.
items.Why CIA is involved: Masking protects confidentiality of sensitive data.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Data leakage prevention
items.Security requirement: Apply DLP measures to systems, networks and devices handling sensitive information.
items.Why CIA is involved: DLP directly protects confidentiality.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Information backup
items.Security requirement: Maintain and regularly test backup copies per agreed policy.
items.Why CIA is involved: Backups protect availability and integrity of data.
items.Evidence to verify: Backup jobs, restore test results, immutability
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
items.Security requirement: Implement sufficient redundancy to meet availability requirements.
items.Why CIA is involved: Redundancy protects availability.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Logging
items.Security requirement: Produce, store, protect and analyse logs of activities, exceptions, faults and events.
items.Why CIA is involved: Logs support integrity of the record and availability for investigation.
items.Evidence to verify: Log sources inventory, log integrity and retention
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Monitoring activities
items.Security requirement: Monitor networks, systems and applications for anomalous behaviour and evaluate potential incidents.
items.Why CIA is involved: Monitoring detects threats across all properties.
items.Evidence to verify: SIEM/SOC use cases, alerts, tuning records
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Clock synchronization
items.Security requirement: Synchronize clocks of information processing systems to approved time sources.
items.Why CIA is involved: Accurate timestamps support integrity of logs/evidence.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Use of privileged utility programs
items.Security requirement: Restrict and tightly control utility programs able to override system controls.
items.Why CIA is involved: Privileged utilities can bypass controls if misused.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Installation of software on operational systems
items.Security requirement: Implement procedures to securely manage software installation on operational systems.
items.Why CIA is involved: Controlled installation maintains system integrity.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Networks security
items.Security requirement: Secure, manage and control networks and network devices.
items.Why CIA is involved: Network security is foundational to all three properties.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Security of network services
items.Security requirement: Identify, implement and monitor security mechanisms, service levels and requirements of network services.
items.Why CIA is involved: Network service security extends this to third-party services.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Segregation of networks
items.Security requirement: Segregate groups of services, users and systems in networks.
items.Why CIA is involved: Segmentation limits exposure/lateral movement.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Web filtering
items.Security requirement: Manage access to external websites to reduce exposure to malicious content.
items.Why CIA is involved: Web filtering reduces exposure to malicious content/data loss.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Use of cryptography
items.Security requirement: Define and implement rules for effective use of cryptography incl. key management.
items.Why CIA is involved: Cryptography protects confidentiality and integrity.
items.Evidence to verify: Crypto policy, key lifecycle, approved algorithms
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Secure development life cycle
items.Security requirement: Establish and apply rules for secure development of software and systems.
items.Why CIA is involved: Secure SDLC embeds security across the lifecycle.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Application security requirements
items.Security requirement: Identify, specify and approve security requirements for applications.
items.Why CIA is involved: Security requirements shape what the application must protect.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
items.Security requirement: Establish, document, maintain and apply secure engineering principles.
items.Why CIA is involved: Secure architecture underpins all three properties.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Secure coding
items.Security requirement: Apply secure coding principles to software development.
items.Why CIA is involved: Secure coding reduces integrity-impacting vulnerabilities.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Security testing in development and acceptance
items.Security requirement: Define and implement security testing in the development life cycle.
items.Why CIA is involved: Security testing validates protection across all properties.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Outsourced development
items.Security requirement: Direct, monitor and review outsourced system development activities.
items.Why CIA is involved: Outsourced development carries the same CIA risks as in-house.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Separation of development, test and production environments
items.Security requirement: Separate and secure development, testing and production environments.
items.Why CIA is involved: Environment separation prevents unintended changes to production integrity.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Change management
items.Security requirement: Subject changes to information processing facilities and systems to change management procedures.
items.Why CIA is involved: Change management protects integrity of systems during change.
items.Evidence to verify: Change tickets, CAB records, rollback plans
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Test information
items.Security requirement: Appropriately select, protect and manage test information.
items.Why CIA is involved: Test data protection avoids exposing live sensitive data.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

items.Title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
items.Security requirement: Plan and agree audit tests and assurance activities to minimize disruption.
items.Why CIA is involved: Audit activity must not compromise confidentiality or availability.
items._section: A.8 - Technological controls

headers: Audit-readiness alignment for the certified organization

items.Title: General
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Certification must inspire confidence: principles of impartiality, competence, responsibility, openness, confidentiality, responsiveness to complaints and risk-based approach underpin all certification activity.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Expect the audit to be conducted objectively and evidence-based; be ready to demonstrate rather than assert conformity.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 4 - Principles (basis for confidence in certification)

items.Title: Impartiality
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB must be impartial and be seen to be; decisions are based on objective evidence, free from conflicts of interest.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Do not offer inducements or influence auditors; separate any consultancy from the certification audit; declare prior consulting relationships.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 4 - Principles (basis for confidence in certification)

items.Title: Competence
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Certification personnel must have the knowledge and skills to perform certification activities for the relevant scope/sector.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Confirm the CB's audit team is competent for your sector, technology (e.g. AI, cloud, telecom) and risk profile before the audit.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: CB team competence evidence, sector/technical-expert confirmation
items._section: Clause 4 - Principles (basis for confidence in certification)

items.Title: Responsibility
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The client organization, not the CB, is responsible for conformity with certification requirements.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Own and maintain the management system continuously; certification is not a substitute for ongoing conformity.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 4 - Principles (basis for confidence in certification)

items.Title: Openness
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB provides appropriate public access to information about its audit process and certification status.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Be aware certification status and scope can be publicly verified; ensure scope wording is accurate.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 4 - Principles (basis for confidence in certification)

items.Title: Confidentiality
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB must protect confidential client information obtained during certification activities.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Confirm confidentiality terms in the certification agreement; control what evidence (logs, architecture, risk registers, model/data details) is shared with auditors and how.
items.Why CIA is involved: Auditors access sensitive security and AI system information; confidentiality obligations and controlled evidence sharing protect it.
items.Evidence to verify: Certification agreement confidentiality clause, evidence-sharing controls
items._section: Clause 4 - Principles (basis for confidence in certification)

items.Title: Responsiveness to complaints
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB responds effectively to complaints and appeals, with fair handling.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Know the CB's complaints/appeals route in case of audit disagreement or contested findings.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 4 - Principles (basis for confidence in certification)

items.Title: Risk-based approach
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB considers risks to impartiality, competence and consistency when planning and decision-making.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Expect audit time and focus to reflect your risk profile; keep risk assessments current and evidence-ready.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 4 - Principles (basis for confidence in certification)

items.Title: Legal and contractual matters
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB is a legal entity and has a legally enforceable certification agreement with each client, defining rights/obligations and responsibility for decisions.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Review and sign the certification agreement; understand obligations (access, notification of changes, mark usage, surveillance cycle).
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 5 - General requirements

items.Title: Management of impartiality
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB identifies, analyses and documents risks to impartiality and has top management commitment to it.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Ensure no undisclosed consultancy or related-party relationship with the CB or audit team.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 5 - General requirements

items.Title: Liability and financing
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB has arrangements (insurance/reserves) to cover liabilities from operations.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Not a client obligation; confirm CB is accredited and in good standing before engaging.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 5 - General requirements

items.Title: Organizational structure and top management
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB documents its organizational structure, duties and authorities; a body/committee safeguards impartiality.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Verify CB accreditation scope covers your standard (e.g. ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001) and sector.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 6 - Structural requirements

items.Title: Operational control
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB has a process for effective control of certification activities carried out by branch offices, partnerships, agents or franchisees.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Confirm the audit is carried out under the CB's controlled process even where delivered locally.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 6 - Structural requirements

items.Title: Competence of personnel
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB defines competence criteria and processes for selecting/monitoring personnel for each management system type and technical area.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Ask for auditor competence for information security, AI management, cloud and telecom-specific technology as applicable.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 7 - Resource requirements

items.Title: Personnel involved in certification activities
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB has sufficient competent personnel (auditors, reviewers, decision-makers); contracts and training are in place.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Be ready to accommodate the assigned audit team; raise any competence concerns before the audit.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 7 - Resource requirements

items.Title: Use of individual external auditors and technical experts
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: External auditors/experts operate under the CB's contract, impartiality and confidentiality requirements.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Confirm external technical experts are bound by confidentiality and conflict-of-interest rules.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 7 - Resource requirements

items.Title: Personnel records
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB maintains up-to-date records of qualifications, training, experience and performance of personnel.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Not a client obligation; you may request evidence of auditor qualifications.
items.Why CIA is involved: CB personnel records contain personal data needing confidentiality and integrity.
items._section: Clause 7 - Resource requirements

items.Title: Outsourcing
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB retains responsibility when outsourcing audit activities and has a legally binding agreement covering confidentiality and impartiality.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Confirm whether any audit activity is outsourced and that outsourcing agreements protect your information.
items.Why CIA is involved: Outsourced audit parties gain access to client information; agreements must protect confidentiality.
items._section: Clause 7 - Resource requirements

items.Title: Public information
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB publicly provides information on its audit processes, certification process, and granting/suspending/withdrawing certification.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Read the CB's published process so audit steps and timelines are expected.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 8 - Information requirements

items.Title: Certification documents
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB gives certification documents identifying the client, standard, scope, and validity.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Verify certificate scope, standard version and validity dates are accurate; report inaccuracies promptly.
items.Why CIA is involved: Certificates are trust artefacts; accuracy and protection from tampering/forgery preserve their integrity.
items.Evidence to verify: Issued certificate verified against scope and SoA
items._section: Clause 8 - Information requirements

items.Title: Reference to certification and use of marks
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB controls use of certification marks; clients must not misuse certification or mislead about scope.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Use marks and certification claims only within the certified scope and per CB rules.
items.Why CIA is involved: Misrepresentation of certification undermines the integrity of the certification claim.
items._section: Clause 8 - Information requirements

items.Title: Confidentiality
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB keeps information about clients confidential, has a legally enforceable commitment, and informs the client before disclosing to third parties unless required by law.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Agree what information can be disclosed to regulators/accreditation bodies; require notification of any legally required disclosure.
items.Why CIA is involved: Direct confidentiality obligation over client security and AI system information.
items._section: Clause 8 - Information requirements

items.Title: Information exchange between a CB and its clients
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB informs clients of certification requirements, changes and audit findings; clients inform the CB of significant changes (scope, ownership, incidents, legal proceedings).
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Establish a channel to notify the CB of significant changes (e.g. major security incidents, scope/organizational changes, new AI systems) and receive CB updates.
items.Why CIA is involved: Exchanged findings, incident and scope information is sensitive and must remain accurate and confidential.
items._section: Clause 8 - Information requirements

items.Title: Pre-certification activities
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Application review, audit programme, audit time determination, multi-site sampling, and combined audits are defined before certification.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Provide accurate scope, sites, headcount, systems and (for AI) AI systems in scope; agree audit programme and time.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Planning audits
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB determines audit objectives, scope and criteria, selects the audit team, and prepares an audit plan; plan is communicated to the client.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Review the audit plan; ensure interviewees, evidence and system access are arranged.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Initial certification audit (Stage 1 and Stage 2)
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Stage 1 reviews documented information and readiness; Stage 2 assesses implementation and effectiveness of the management system.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Have documented information, risk assessment, SoA, internal audit and management review completed before Stage 1; controls operating with evidence before Stage 2.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Stage 1 documentation pack, Stage 2 operating evidence
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Conducting audits
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Opening/closing meetings, evidence gathering and verification, recording findings (nonconformities and opportunities for improvement), audit report, cause analysis of nonconformities and verification of corrections/corrective actions.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Provide access and evidence; agree findings; submit cause analysis and corrective action plans within CB timelines.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Audit evidence, corrective action plans, root-cause analyses
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Certification decision
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Decision is made by persons not involved in the audit, based on audit report and other information; certification granted, refused or deferred.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Do not expect a decision at the closing meeting; ensure all major nonconformities are closed within required time.
items.Why CIA is involved: The decision must rest on accurate, untampered audit information and impartial review.
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Maintaining certification
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Surveillance audits, recertification audits, special audits and suspension/withdrawal processes maintain certification over the cycle.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Keep the ISMS/AIMS operating between audits: internal audits, management reviews, incident handling and change control must continue; prepare for surveillance.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Surveillance-cycle plan, internal audit and management review records
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Appeals
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB has a documented process to receive, evaluate and decide appeals; appeal decisions do not lead to discrimination.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Know the appeals process if you disagree with a certification decision.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Complaints
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB handles complaints about its own activities and about certified clients, with confidentiality.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Be prepared to respond if a complaint concerns your certified system; maintain your own complaints/incident handling.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Client records
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB maintains records of audit and certification for all clients, kept confidential and retained per policy.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Retain your own copies of audit reports, findings and closure evidence; treat them as confidential.
items.Why CIA is involved: Audit and certification records hold sensitive findings; they must be protected (C), accurate (I) and available for the certification cycle (A).
items.Evidence to verify: Records retention and access-control rules for audit records
items._section: Clause 9 - Process requirements

items.Title: Options
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB implements a management system per Option A (own requirements) or Option B (ISO 9001).
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Informational: the CB's own management system is audited by its accreditation body.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option A - General
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB establishes, documents, implements and maintains a management system capable of consistent achievement of its requirements.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Informational for clients.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option A - Management system manual
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Documents the management system policies and procedures.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Informational for clients.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option A - Control of documents
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Controls documents so current versions are available and obsolete ones are prevented from use.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Mirrors your own documented-information control; apply the same discipline to your ISMS/AIMS documents.
items.Why CIA is involved: Document control preserves integrity of policies and procedures.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option A - Control of records
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Maintains records demonstrating conformity, protected, retrievable and retained.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Mirrors your own records control; audit evidence must be retrievable and reliable.
items.Why CIA is involved: Records must stay unaltered (I) and retrievable for audit (A).
items.Evidence to verify: Records retention schedule, backups of evidence
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option A - Management review
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: Top management reviews the CB's management system at planned intervals.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Mirrors your own management review requirement.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option A - Internal audits
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB conducts internal audits at planned intervals.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Mirrors your own internal audit requirement; CBs expect one completed before the initial audit.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option A - Corrective actions
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB identifies and manages nonconformities and takes corrective action.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Mirrors your nonconformity/corrective action process.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option A - Preventive actions
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB takes actions to eliminate causes of potential nonconformities (risk-based).
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Mirrors risk-based preventive thinking in your risk treatment.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

items.Title: Option B - Management system per ISO 9001
items.Certification body (CB) requirement: The CB may instead implement a quality management system per ISO 9001.
items.Audit-readiness alignment for the certif: Informational for clients.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies

headers: Security note / why CIA is involved

items.Title: Material and territorial scope
items.Requirement: Determine applicability: processing of personal data wholly/partly by automated means, and territorial scope incl. non-EU controllers/processors offering goods/services to or monitoring EU data subjects.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter I - General provisions

items.Title: Definitions
items.Requirement: Apply GDPR definitions consistently (personal data, processing, controller, processor, consent, special categories, pseudonymisation, etc.).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter I - General provisions

items.Title: Principles relating to processing
items.Requirement: Process personal data lawfully, fairly, transparently; for specified/legitimate purposes; data minimisation; accuracy; storage limitation; integrity and confidentiality; and demonstrate compliance (accountability).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: 'Integrity and confidentiality' is an explicit principle: personal data must be processed with appropriate security against unauthorised/unlawful processing, accidental loss, destruction or damage.
items.Evidence to verify: Data protection policy covering all principles
items._section: Chapter II - Principles

items.Title: Accountability
items.Requirement: The controller is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate, compliance with the principles.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Records of processing, policies, evidence of compliance mechanisms
items._section: Chapter II - Principles

items.Title: Lawfulness of processing
items.Requirement: Identify and document a valid legal basis for each processing activity (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter II - Principles

items.Title: Conditions for consent
items.Requirement: Where relying on consent, ensure it is freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, demonstrable, and as easy to withdraw as to give.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter II - Principles

items.Title: Conditions for children's consent
items.Requirement: Apply age-of-consent rules for information society services offered directly to children, incl. parental consent verification where required.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter II - Principles

items.Title: Special categories of personal data
items.Requirement: Do not process special-category data (health, biometric, genetic, racial/ethnic origin, etc.) unless an Article 9(2) condition applies; apply enhanced safeguards.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Special-category data needs enhanced confidentiality safeguards given the higher sensitivity/harm from disclosure.
items.Evidence to verify: Special-category processing register and conditions relied on
items._section: Chapter II - Principles

items.Title: Processing of criminal conviction/offence data
items.Requirement: Only process such data under official authority or with appropriate safeguards.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Sensitive data requiring confidentiality safeguards.
items.Evidence to verify: Legal basis and safeguards for criminal-data processing
items._section: Chapter II - Principles

items.Title: Transparency and information to data subjects
items.Requirement: Provide concise, transparent, intelligible information about processing (privacy notices) at the point of collection or within required timeframes.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Right of access
items.Requirement: Provide data subjects, on request, confirmation of processing and a copy of their personal data plus specified information, within one month.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Subject access request (SAR) procedure and log
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Right to rectification
items.Requirement: Allow data subjects to have inaccurate personal data corrected without undue delay.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Correcting inaccurate data restores the integrity of the personal data held.
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
items.Requirement: Erase personal data without undue delay where a listed ground applies (no longer necessary, consent withdrawn, unlawful processing, etc.), subject to exemptions.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Right to restriction of processing
items.Requirement: Restrict processing in specified circumstances (e.g. accuracy contested, processing unlawful) while a matter is resolved.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Notification obligation re rectification/erasure/restriction
items.Requirement: Notify each recipient to whom data was disclosed of rectification/erasure/restriction, unless impossible or disproportionate.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Right to data portability
items.Requirement: Provide personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and enable transmission to another controller where technically feasible.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Right to object
items.Requirement: Allow objection to processing based on legitimate interests/public task, and to direct marketing (absolute right).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
items.Requirement: Do not base decisions with legal/similarly significant effect solely on automated processing (incl. profiling) unless an exception applies; provide safeguards incl. human intervention and right to contest.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject

items.Title: Responsibility of the controller
items.Requirement: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and demonstrate processing complies with the Regulation, proportionate to risk.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Foundational obligation to implement security/organisational measures protecting personal data across CIA.
items._section: Chapter IV S1 - Controller and processor obligations

items.Title: Data protection by design and by default
items.Requirement: Implement data protection principles (e.g. pseudonymisation, minimisation) by design at the time of determining processing means, and by default ensure only necessary data is processed.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Minimisation and pseudonymisation by design/default directly reduce confidentiality exposure.
items._section: Chapter IV S1 - Controller and processor obligations

items.Title: Joint controllers
items.Requirement: Determine and transparently document respective responsibilities of joint controllers via an arrangement.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter IV S1 - Controller and processor obligations

items.Title: Representatives of controllers/processors not established in the Union
items.Requirement: Designate an EU representative where required by territorial scope.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter IV S1 - Controller and processor obligations

items.Title: Processor
items.Requirement: Use only processors providing sufficient guarantees; govern processing via a binding contract (DPA) covering subject matter, duration, nature, purpose, data types, obligations incl. security, sub-processor rules, and audit rights.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: DPAs must require the processor to implement Article 32 security measures protecting confidentiality, integrity and availability of the data it processes.
items.Evidence to verify: Data processing agreements (DPAs) with all processors
items._section: Chapter IV S1 - Controller and processor obligations

items.Title: Processing under the authority of the controller or processor
items.Requirement: Ensure persons processing data under the controller's/processor's authority do so only on instructions, unless required by law.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Limits who can access personal data, protecting confidentiality.
items._section: Chapter IV S1 - Controller and processor obligations

items.Title: Records of processing activities
items.Requirement: Maintain records of processing activities (ROPA) covering purposes, categories of data/subjects, recipients, transfers, retention periods and security measures.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter IV S1 - Controller and processor obligations

items.Title: Cooperation with the supervisory authority
items.Requirement: Cooperate with the supervisory authority on request in the performance of its tasks.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter IV S1 - Controller and processor obligations

items.Title: Security of processing
items.Requirement: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to risk: pseudonymisation/encryption; ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of systems; ability to restore availability/access after an incident; regular testing/evaluation of measures.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: This is GDPR's core cybersecurity article - it explicitly names confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience as the required security outcomes.
items.Evidence to verify: Security policy, encryption/pseudonymisation controls, resilience/DR testing, security testing reports
items._section: Chapter IV S2 - Security of personal data

items.Title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
items.Requirement: Notify the supervisory authority without undue delay, and where feasible within 72 hours, of becoming aware of a personal data breach, unless unlikely to result in risk; document all breaches.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Breach response protects against further loss of confidentiality/integrity/availability and is triggered specifically by CIA-impacting events.
items.Evidence to verify: Breach notification procedure, breach register, notifications sent
items._section: Chapter IV S2 - Security of personal data

items.Title: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
items.Requirement: Communicate the breach to affected data subjects without undue delay when it is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Follows directly from a confidentiality/integrity/availability-impacting breach.
items.Evidence to verify: Data-subject breach notifications, risk assessment of breach
items._section: Chapter IV S2 - Security of personal data

items.Title: Data protection impact assessment (DPIA)
items.Requirement: Carry out a DPIA before processing likely to result in high risk to individuals (e.g. large-scale special-category processing, systematic monitoring, new technology incl. AI); describe processing, necessity/proportionality, risks, and measures to address them.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: DPIAs must assess and mitigate confidentiality/privacy risks to individuals from the processing.
items._section: Chapter IV S3 - Data protection impact assessment and prior consultation

items.Title: Prior consultation
items.Requirement: Consult the supervisory authority prior to processing where a DPIA indicates high residual risk that cannot be mitigated.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter IV S3 - Data protection impact assessment and prior consultation

items.Title: Designation of the data protection officer
items.Requirement: Designate a DPO where required (public authority, large-scale regular/systematic monitoring, or large-scale special-category processing); publish contact details and notify the supervisory authority.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: DPO appointment record, published contact details
items._section: Chapter IV S4 - Data protection officer

items.Title: Position of the DPO
items.Requirement: Involve the DPO properly and in a timely manner in all data protection matters; provide resources and independence; DPO reports to highest management level.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter IV S4 - Data protection officer

items.Title: Tasks of the DPO
items.Requirement: DPO informs/advises on obligations, monitors compliance, advises on DPIAs, cooperates with and acts as contact point for the supervisory authority.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter IV S4 - Data protection officer

items.Title: General principle for transfers / adequacy decisions
items.Requirement: Transfer personal data outside the EEA only where an adequacy decision applies or another Chapter V mechanism is used.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter V - Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

items.Title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
items.Requirement: Absent adequacy, use appropriate safeguards (e.g. Standard Contractual Clauses, Binding Corporate Rules) providing enforceable rights and effective remedies.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: Cross-border transfer safeguards protect confidentiality of personal data once it leaves the EEA's legal protections.
items._section: Chapter V - Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

items.Title: Derogations for specific situations
items.Requirement: Rely on derogations (explicit consent, contract necessity, public interest, etc.) only where Article 46 mechanisms are unavailable and conditions are met.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter V - Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

items.Title: Right to compensation and liability
items.Requirement: Data subjects have the right to compensation for material or non-material damage from an infringement; controllers/processors are liable unless not responsible for the event.
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter VIII - Remedies, liability and penalties

items.Title: Administrative fines
items.Requirement: Ensure compliance to avoid fines (tiered, up to the higher of EUR 20m or 4% of global annual turnover for the most serious infringements).
items.Security note / why CIA is involved: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Chapter VIII - Remedies, liability and penalties

items.Description: Crafted inputs (direct or indirect, via untrusted content the model retrieves/ingests) override or manipulate the model's instructions, causing unintended actions, data exposure or policy violations.
items.Mitigations: Enforce privilege control on LLM access to backend systems; segregate/mark external content; require human approval for high-risk actions; adversarial/red-team testing; input/output filtering.
items.Why CIA is involved: Can be used to exfiltrate data (C), manipulate outputs/actions (I), or trigger disruptive/unbounded actions (A) depending on what the model is connected to.
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: The model inadvertently exposes PII, credentials, proprietary data or confidential business information present in training data, context or connected systems.
items.Mitigations: Data sanitization/redaction; strict access controls on data the model can reach; differential privacy/federated learning where applicable; conceal system prompts; output filtering for sensitive patterns.
items.Why CIA is involved: Direct confidentiality risk - unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data through model output.
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: Compromised or vulnerable components in the LLM supply chain - pre-trained models, fine-tuning adapters (e.g. LoRA), datasets, plugins and deployment platforms - introduce vulnerabilities, backdoors or bias.
items.Mitigations: Vet data/model sources and suppliers; vulnerability scanning of models/dependencies; maintain an AI/ML Bill of Materials (SBOM/MLBOM); use verifiable model provenance and integrity checks; monitor collaborative development platforms.
items.Why CIA is involved: A compromised supply-chain component can leak data (C), alter model behaviour (I) or disable the service (A).
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: Manipulation of training, fine-tuning or embedding data introduces vulnerabilities, backdoors or biases that compromise the model's security, effectiveness or ethical behaviour.
items.Mitigations: Track data lineage/provenance; vet data vendors; strict sandboxing of training pipelines; use data version control (DVC); red-team for poisoning; monitor training loss/behaviour for anomalies.
items.Why CIA is involved: Poisoning directly corrupts the integrity of the model's learned behaviour.
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: Insufficient validation, sanitization or escaping of LLM output before it is passed to downstream systems, enabling XSS, CSRF, SSRF, privilege escalation or remote code execution.
items.Mitigations: Treat model output as untrusted input; apply context-aware output encoding/sanitization; validate before executing/rendering; least-privilege execution of any downstream action.
items.Why CIA is involved: Unvalidated output can corrupt downstream systems (I) or be used to trigger disruptive actions (A) via the systems that consume it.
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: An LLM-based agent is granted excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy, allowing it to take damaging actions beyond what the task requires, especially when combined with prompt injection.
items.Mitigations: Apply least-privilege scoping of tools/functions/plugins; require human approval for consequential actions; limit autonomous action chains; log and monitor agent actions; use sandboxed execution environments.
items.Why CIA is involved: An over-privileged agent can be manipulated into unauthorized disclosure (C), unintended changes (I) or destructive/disruptive actions (A).
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: Attackers extract the hidden system prompt, exposing internal instructions, business logic, credentials or guardrail design that can then be used to bypass safeguards.
items.Mitigations: Avoid placing secrets/credentials in system prompts; treat system prompts as sensitive but not as a security boundary; use out-of-band guardrails independent of the prompt; test for extraction via red-teaming.
items.Why CIA is involved: Direct confidentiality risk to the operator's internal instructions and any embedded secrets.
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: Weaknesses in how vectors/embeddings are generated, stored, or retrieved (e.g. in RAG pipelines) allow injection of malicious content, data poisoning of the knowledge base, or unauthorized retrieval of restricted data.
items.Mitigations: Apply access controls/permissions on the vector store per document sensitivity; validate/sanitize ingested content before embedding; monitor retrieval patterns; isolate multi-tenant vector stores.
items.Why CIA is involved: Retrieval-store weaknesses can expose data across access boundaries (C) or let injected content corrupt retrieved context (I).
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: The model produces confident but false or misleading output (hallucination), which users or downstream systems may treat as reliable, leading to harmful decisions, legal exposure or reputational damage.
items.Mitigations: Ground outputs with retrieval/citation (RAG) and require source attribution; implement automated fact-checking/cross-verification; communicate limitations to users; human review for high-stakes outputs.
items.Why CIA is involved: Misinformation is fundamentally an integrity failure - the output does not reliably reflect truth or the intended knowledge base.
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Description: Uncontrolled or excessive inference requests (denial of wallet/service, resource exhaustion) degrade availability or cause uncontrolled cost, incl. via model extraction through repeated querying.
items.Mitigations: Rate limiting and quotas per user/API key; input/output size limits; monitor for abnormal usage patterns; cost alerting and circuit breakers; watermarking/output limits to deter model extraction.
items.Why CIA is involved: Directly an availability and resource-exhaustion risk, with a confidentiality dimension when used for model extraction.
items.Evidence to verify: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

items.Title: Context of the organization (privacy extension)
items.Requirement / guidance: Extend ISO 27001 4.1-4.4 to consider the organization's role (PII controller and/or processor), applicable privacy laws/regulations (e.g. GDPR, PDPPL), and interested parties relevant to PII processing.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - privacy governance/rights-based requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: PIMS scope statement identifying controller/processor role(s) and applicable privacy law
items._section: Clause 5 - PIMS-specific requirements related to ISO/IEC 27001 (extends ISMS clauses 4-10 to privacy)

items.Title: Leadership (privacy extension)
items.Requirement / guidance: Extend ISO 27001 5.1-5.3 so the information security policy is extended (or a separate privacy policy established) with privacy roles and responsibilities assigned.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - privacy governance/rights-based requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 5 - PIMS-specific requirements related to ISO/IEC 27001 (extends ISMS clauses 4-10 to privacy)

items.Title: Planning (privacy extension) - privacy risk assessment
items.Requirement / guidance: Extend the ISO 27001 risk assessment (6.1.2) to consider risks associated with the processing of PII to both the organization and to PII principals; extend risk treatment (6.1.3) and produce a PIMS Statement of Applicability referencing Annex A/B.
items.Why CIA is involved: Privacy risk assessment specifically evaluates confidentiality/exposure risk to individuals from PII processing.
items.Evidence to verify: Privacy risk assessment methodology and register, PIMS SoA
items._section: Clause 5 - PIMS-specific requirements related to ISO/IEC 27001 (extends ISMS clauses 4-10 to privacy)

items.Title: Support (privacy extension)
items.Requirement / guidance: Extend ISO 27001 7.x so resources, competence, awareness, communication and documented information also cover the PIMS.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - privacy governance/rights-based requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: Privacy training records, PIMS documentation set
items._section: Clause 5 - PIMS-specific requirements related to ISO/IEC 27001 (extends ISMS clauses 4-10 to privacy)

items.Title: Operation (privacy extension)
items.Requirement / guidance: Extend ISO 27001 8.1-8.3 operational planning/control and risk assessment/treatment to privacy risks arising from operating the PIMS.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - privacy governance/rights-based requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items._section: Clause 5 - PIMS-specific requirements related to ISO/IEC 27001 (extends ISMS clauses 4-10 to privacy)

items.Title: Performance evaluation (privacy extension)
items.Requirement / guidance: Extend ISO 27001 9.1-9.3 monitoring, internal audit and management review to cover PIMS conformity and effectiveness.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - privacy governance/rights-based requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
items.Evidence to verify: PIMS-inclusive internal audit and management review records
items._section: Clause 5 - PIMS-specific requirements related to ISO/IEC 27001 (extends ISMS clauses 4-10 to privacy)

items.Title: Improvement (privacy extension)
items.Requirement / guidance: Extend ISO 27001 10.1-10.2 continual improvement and corrective action to nonconformities affecting the PIMS.
items.Why CIA is involved: None - privacy governance/rights-based requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
